The Hidden Life of Octopuses

By Jane Marlowe — September 12, 2025

Octopuses have long fascinated biologists. With nine brains, three hearts, and the ability to change color and texture in milliseconds, they seem more like aliens than animals from this planet. Recent research suggests their cognitive abilities rival those of small mammals.

In the lab, an octopus named Inky famously escaped a New Zealand aquarium in 2016 by squeezing through a drainpipe to the ocean. Stories like Inky's hint at problem-solving abilities far beyond instinctive behavior. Researchers now believe octopuses can recognize individual humans, hold grudges, and engage in play with novel objects.

But what does it feel like to be an octopus? Philosophers and neuroscientists alike have grappled with this question, since their distributed nervous systems suggest a kind of cognition unlike anything in vertebrates.
